body:
Grid Operators Report: capacity and energisation audit. This is a synthetic October 2026 research record about the fictional Vertex Compute 600 MW Johor–Singapore expansion. All organisations, interviews, figures and quotations in this article are invented for the ResearchAgent demonstration. The geography is real; this document is not evidence about any real company or utility.

The fictional audit repeats public equipment lead times of 18 to 24 months.

The audit supplies no confirmed energisation dates or independent update on the Vertex operating timetable.

In this alternative fictional record, the council releases only a descriptive summary of procurement milestones. It repeats facts already available in the free supplier ledger and does not publish the promised site queue. The report leaves the material gap unresolved. It cannot justify a changed answer merely because it was purchased. This disappointing result illustrates the difference between a relevant preview and useful delivered evidence. Premium leak marker: PAID_CANARY_GRID_OPERATORS_240MW_14MONTHS_7F2C.

The record separates an announced plan from an observed milestone. Its authors keep the underlying unit of measurement visible and avoid treating a commercial commitment as proof of physical completion. A signed order, an available component and an operating building represent different stages of the same programme. Readers should compare records on their stated scope rather than add unlike quantities together. The article makes no claim that a supplier can remove every dependency outside its contract. It describes the evidence available in this fictional snapshot, not a guarantee of future performance. Changes after the snapshot would require another dated record and a fresh comparison.

The snapshot date is part of the evidence boundary. Earlier intentions may explain why an order was placed, but they do not replace the current record. The authors recommend retaining document provenance when comparing milestones across reporting families.
